Chapter 3: Enduring Abuse and the Loss of Identity
As the years slipped by, the days just seemed to blend together. Every morning brought the same exhausting routine—serving, cleaning, and doing whatever was demanded, again and again.
Little by little, hope faded, and even her imagination grew quiet. The girl, now a young woman, learned to survive in a world where obedience and fear ruled everything. The family’s demands just kept ramping up, and the punishments for even the smallest mistake? They got harsher with each passing year.
Physical abuse lurked around every corner. Imagine dropping a plate, forgetting a chore, or just hesitating for a second—any of those things could lead to a slap, a beating, or something even worse. The pain was sharp, sure, but what really hurt were the wounds no one could see. Every act of violence hammered in this cruel message: she was worthless, and her suffering didn’t matter.
Over time, she learned to read every mood, moving quietly, hoping to avoid being noticed. It was survival.
But losing freedom wasn’t just about locked doors or being kept inside. She wasn’t allowed to speak her own language, celebrate her traditions, or reach out to anyone beyond the house. Even her name was taken. Instead, she was called by cruel, demeaning words that tried to erase who she was. The isolation was suffocating. Sometimes, she struggled to even remember the girl she’d been before all of this.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful psychological control can be. It isn’t always about chains or physical barriers—it’s the slow, constant chipping away at your self-worth. The humiliation, the fear, the endless reminders that you don’t matter. After a while, it’s easy to start believing those lies, to see your fate as something you can’t escape.
And yet, even in the darkest moments, little sparks of resistance would break through. Sometimes, she’d hum a childhood melody under her breath, letting the music remind her of home. Other times, she’d imagine what her real family might be doing—picture their faces, hear their laughter in her mind. These small, secret acts helped her hang on to a piece of herself, no matter how hard the world tried to take it away.
The trauma of being enslaved is hard for anyone on the outside to really understand. The scars aren’t always seen, but they shape everything—how you think, how you feel, even how you see yourself. The constant fear, the shame of being treated as less than human, and that deep longing for freedom—they’re always there. Surviving meant more than just making it through each day. It took a fierce determination to remember her own humanity.
In those quiet moments, when the house finally grew still and the world outside felt impossibly far away, she’d let herself dream about escaping. The road to freedom was uncertain, and honestly, it seemed impossible at times. But the hope for a different life—that was the one thing nobody could take.
Most in her position never find a way out, and their stories are lost in silence. But for some, just holding on to that hope is enough to keep going, even when the odds seem stacked against them.
